questions.question: What is particulate matter in air?
choices: Only gas molecules released by combustion
Water vapor remaining entirely gaseous
Suspended solid particles and liquid droplets
Only the visible color of outdoor air

questions.question: What is a primary air pollutant?
choices: A pollutant formed only after atmospheric reactions
A pollutant emitted directly from a source
A pollutant measured only indoors
A pollutant defined by being the most abundant

questions.question: What is a secondary air pollutant?
choices: A pollutant emitted unchanged directly from a source
A pollutant defined only by low concentration
A pollutant produced only at nighttime
A pollutant formed through reactions in the atmosphere

questions.question: What is a temperature inversion?
choices: A layer in which temperature increases with height, limiting some vertical mixing
A layer that always enhances vertical mixing
A condition where temperature decreases rapidly with height
A sudden change in wind direction without temperature change

questions.question: What is ventilation intended to do in an indoor space?
choices: Exchange air and help reduce contaminant buildup
Only recirculating air without any pollutant removal or exchange
Guaranteeing that all indoor surfaces are sterile
Keeping every pollutant trapped inside a room

questions.question: Which gas can form from incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels?
choices: Nitrogen as the only product
Helium
Carbon monoxide
Argon

questions.question: Which is a common source of fine particle pollution?
choices: The motion of clean air without particles
Combustion smoke
Only the evaporation of pure water
Only the normal oxygen content of air

questions.question: Why can ground-level ozone be harmful while stratospheric ozone is protective?
choices: The two locations contain different chemical elements
Ozone has identical effects regardless of exposure location
Upper-atmosphere ozone mainly filters visible rather than ultraviolet light
Its effects depend on location: inhaled ozone harms tissues, while upper ozone absorbs UV

questions.question: How does much ground-level ozone form?
choices: The evaporation of pure water without any chemical reaction
Sunlight-driven reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds
Emission of all ground-level ozone directly from vehicle exhausts
The direct release of ozone whenever nitrogen gas cools

questions.question: Why can inversions worsen local air pollution?
choices: They can trap pollutants near the surface by limiting mixing
They necessarily reduce every source's emissions
They always strengthen upward air mixing
They remove particles by creating cleaner oxygen

questions.question: Why can air pollution travel across regional boundaries?
choices: All pollutants stop at regional boundaries
Only sources inside a region can affect its air
Winds can transport pollutants and their precursors
Transported precursors cannot form pollutants later

questions.question: Why is absence of a visible haze insufficient evidence of clean air?
choices: Every pollutant has a visible color
Air without haze contains no particulate matter
Only visible particles influence air quality
Some pollutants are invisible

questions.question: Why can indoor air quality differ from outdoor air quality?
choices: Indoor sources and ventilation affect pollutant concentrations
Outdoor pollutants can never enter buildings
Ventilation has no effect on indoor concentrations
Indoor sources cannot affect air composition

questions.question: Why should an air-monitoring station's location be documented?
choices: All monitoring locations represent every region equally
Location records make calibration unnecessary
Nearby emissions cannot affect a monitor's readings
Nearby sources and surroundings influence measurements

questions.question: Why can reducing pollutant emissions improve air quality?
choices: Emissions reductions guarantee identical weather
Fewer pollutants or precursors enter the atmosphere
Natural sources must disappear when human emissions decrease
Pollutant concentrations depend only on temperature

questions.question: A monitor near a busy road reads higher pollution than a rural monitor. What is a cautious interpretation?
choices: Traffic is proven to be the only possible source
The rural site contains no pollutants
Traffic-related emissions may contribute, but other differences should also be examined
The instruments must measure different units

questions.question: A sunny afternoon follows a morning with substantial ozone-precursor emissions. What pollutant formation is plausible?
choices: Formation of ozone only in the stratosphere
Guaranteed removal of all fine particles
No atmospheric reactions because sunlight is present
Increased ground-level ozone

questions.question: A stable inversion persists over a city. What change may help disperse accumulated pollutants?
choices: Further suppression of vertical mixing
A continued increase in local emissions
Stronger mixing that breaks the inversion
Closing every outdoor monitoring station

questions.question: Two air samples are compared using different instruments with unchecked calibration. What is a concern?
choices: Instrument differences could contribute to the apparent concentration difference
Calibration has no effect on readings
Any difference proves a real change in air quality
Sampling methods cannot influence comparisons

questions.question: A region records fewer pollution peaks after emission controls, but weather also changes. What strengthens the evaluation?
choices: Attribute every change to controls without comparison
Compare longer records while accounting for weather and other factors
Use only the single lowest reading
Ignore all data from before the controls
